claim: Training 500 parallel agents with AMP+teacher-student in Isaac Gym for quadruped bipedal locomotion required 26,000 iterations and 15.88 hours on a single NVIDIA RTX 4070 GPU.
stance_target: AMP training budgets for legged locomotion on single mid-range consumer GPU
scope_conditions: Unitree A1 quadruped in bipedal mode, 6 terrain types, Isaac Gym, teacher-student+AMP framework
quoted_support: 'We trained 500 parallel agents on different types of terrains with increasing difficulties using the Isaac Gym simulator in overall 26000 iterations and cost 15.88 hours in total. All training's were performed on a single NVIDIA RTX 4070 GPU.'

claim: The AMP discriminator state for quadruped bipedal locomotion is 31-dimensional, comprising joint positions, point velocities, base linear velocity, base angular velocity, and base height relative to terrain.
stance_target: AMP discriminator observation space design for legged robots
quoted_support: 'Each state S_t^AMP in R^31 includes joint positions, point velocities, base linear velocity, base angular velocity, and base height relative to the terrain.'

claim: The AMP discriminator training uses a gradient penalty term with coefficient alpha_qp=10 to enforce smoothness.
scope_conditions: AMP for bipedal quadruped locomotion, LSGAN formulation

claim: The style reward in AMP is computed as max[0, 1 - 0.25*(D_phi(s_t, s_{t+1}) - 1)^2], mapping discriminator output to a bounded [0,1] reward signal.
stance_target: AMP style reward formula for policy training
quoted_support: 'r_t^s[(s_t, s_{t+1}) ~ A] = max[0, 1 - 0.25(d^score_t - 1)^2], where d^score_t = D_phi(s_t, s_{t+1}) and is scaled to the range [0,1].'

claim: The AMP reference dataset for bipedal locomotion consists of TO-generated trajectories (forward walking and two running gaits), each lasting 2.4 seconds.
stance_target: Demo dataset size requirements for AMP training
scope_conditions: Unitree A1 biped mode, TOWR trajectory optimizer
quoted_support: 'Our generated trajectories encompass various locomotion patterns, including forward walking and two distinct running gaits, each lasting 2.4 seconds.'

claim: The AMP-trained bipedal quadruped policy achieves 82-93% success rate on flat terrain and 84-91% on stairs at 0.5 m/s, deployed in simulation only (no real robot transfer reported in this paper).
stance_target: AMP policy performance for bipedal legged locomotion
scope_conditions: Unitree A1 biped, Isaac Gym simulation, 6 terrain types, 4 speeds
quoted_support: 'Terrain Types: Uniform, Wave, Stepping Stones, Sloped, Stairs, Obstacles. 0.5 m/s: Acc(%) 77.67-82.76, Succ(%) 84.21-92.3'
numbers: 92.3% success on uniform terrain at 0.5 m/s
84.21% success on sloped terrain at 0.5 m/s

claim: No BC pretrain stage is described; the bipedal AMP paper goes directly from random init to AMP+PPO training in a single 15.88-hour session with no staged curriculum breakdown.
stance_target: Absence of BC pretraining in some AMP pipelines
quoted_support: Section III-B-3 describes only: 'We trained 500 parallel agents... in overall 26000 iterations... 15.88 hours.' No pretrain phase mentioned.

claim: Domain randomization parameters for AMP legged locomotion include link mass [0.8, 1.2]x nominal, payload mass [0, 3] kg, ground friction [0.05, 2.75], restitution [0.0, 1.0], and joint Kp/Kd scaling [0.8, 1.2].
stance_target: Domain randomization ranges for sim-to-real transfer in legged locomotion
quoted_support: Table I: 'Link Mass [0.8, 1.2] kg, Payload Mass [0, 3] kg, Ground Friction [0.05, 2.75], Ground Restitution [0.0, 1.0], Joint Kp [0.8, 1.2] x 20, Joint Kd [0.8, 1.2] x 0.5'
